findings.old_behavior: Interface version v11 exported from lmnet.so
findings.new_behavior: Interface version v12 with 3 new vtable entries (addAllowedSenderEntry, DestructAllowedSenders, isAllowedSenderList) inserted in the middle of the function pointer table
findings.compatibility_reason: Any rsyslog loadable module compiled against interface v11 will fail the runtime version check (pIf->ifVersion != netCURR_IF_VERSION -> RS_RET_INTERFACE_NOT_SUPPORTED) when loaded against the v12 runtime. External plugins and dynamically loaded modules must be recompiled against the new headers.

evidence.snippet:
rsRetVal (*addAllowedSenderEntry)(struct AllowedSenders **ppRoot, struct AllowedSenders **ppLast, uchar *pszAllowedSender);
void (*DestructAllowedSenders)(struct AllowedSenders **ppRoot);
int (*isAllowedSenderList)(struct AllowedSenders *pAllowRoot, struct sockaddr *pFrom, const char *pszFromHost, int bChkDNS);
#define netCURR_IF_VERSION 12 /* increment whenever you change the interface structure! */

findings.why_not_internal_only: runtime/net.h is a public header installed with the rsyslog development package; the interface version is checked by all modules using the net interface; version mismatch causes graceful failure
findings.uncertainty: Low - the interface version change is explicit and version-gated. The new entries are inserted between existing ones, shifting all subsequent offsets.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that all external plugins/modules referencing the net interface are recompiled against the new headers
findings.test_recommendation: Compile a test module against the old v11 interface headers and verify it gracefully fails with RS_RET_INTERFACE_NOT_SUPPORTED when loaded against the v12 runtime

findings.old_behavior: tcpLstnParams_s struct has 13 fields ending with pszRatelimitName
findings.new_behavior: tcpLstnParams_s struct has 15 fields: pAllowedSenderRoot and bUseLegacyAllowedSender appended at the end. The struct size increases by sizeof(pointer) + sizeof(sbool).
findings.compatibility_reason: The tcpLstnParams_s struct defined in runtime/tcpsrv.h is part of the rsyslog runtime public API. The struct is allocated by callers (imtcp, imudp modules) and passed by pointer to tcpsrv via configureTCPListen(). Any code that sizeof() or manually allocates this struct must be recompiled. The struct is used as an opaque parameter in most cases, but external modules that directly access its fields or allocate it statically will observe ABI incompatibility.

evidence.snippet:
struct AllowedSenders *pAllowedSenderRoot; /**< source-address ACL list */
    sbool bUseLegacyAllowedSender; /**< if true, use protocol-global legacy ACLs */

findings.why_not_internal_only: runtime/tcpsrv.h is a public header in the runtime library; tcpLstnParams_s is documented as caller-allocated struct with ownership transfer to tcpsrv
findings.uncertainty: Medium - the fields are appended at the end of the struct, which reduces binary breakage risk. However the struct is in a public installed header and sizeof changes.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no external consumers of the tcpsrv API directly access tcpLstnParams_s fields or allocate the struct statically
findings.test_recommendation: Write a minimal test that allocates tcpLstnParams_t, passes it to configureTCPListen, and verifies the new fields are properly handled

findings.old_behavior: imtcp and imudp modules only consulted the legacy protocol-wide $AllowedSender directive for source address ACL filtering
findings.new_behavior: imtcp and imudp modules accept a new "allowedsender" array parameter at both module level and input instance level. Module-level lists act as defaults for inputs. Input-level lists override the module default. Empty YAML arrays are rejected with RS_RET_INVALID_PARAMS instead of silently clearing filtering. When allowedsender is absent, legacy $AllowedSender behavior is fully preserved.
findings.compatibility_reason: This is an additive config language extension. Existing configs without the allowedsender parameter continue to work identically. The change is backward compatible but introduces new config syntax and new error messages for empty arrays.
findings.why_not_internal_only: Configuration keys define the user-visible rsyslog.conf and YAML config language surface
findings.uncertainty: Low - new parameter is purely additive with explicit legacy path preservation
findings.recommended_review: Document the new allowedsender parameter and its interaction with legacy $AllowedSender directive
findings.test_recommendation: Run the dedicated test scripts: allowed-sender-modern.sh, yaml-allowed-sender-modern.sh, allowed-sender-empty-array.sh

findings.affected_surface: Runtime ACL dispatch in receive paths
findings.old_behavior: processPacket unconditionally called net.isAllowedSender2() for ACL checking, which used the legacy global $AllowedSender list
findings.new_behavior: processPacket conditionally dispatches to either net.isAllowedSender2() (legacy path when bUseLegacyAllowedSender=1) or net.isAllowedSenderList() (modern path with per-instance pAllowedSenderRoot). ACL caching is now invalidated per-listener in addition to per-sender address.
findings.compatibility_reason: The receive-path ACL dispatch logic changed. For existing configs without allowedsender, bUseLegacyAllowedSender defaults to true preserving legacy behavior. However, ACL caching semantics changed (cache invalidation per-listener) which affects how often ACL re-evaluation occurs in multi-listener setups.
findings.why_not_internal_only: ACL enforcement affects which syslog messages are accepted/rejected, directly impacting network security policy
findings.uncertainty: Medium - default preserves legacy, but edge cases with mixed legacy+modern configs may interact unexpectedly
findings.recommended_review: Verify ACL behavior in configurations using both legacy $AllowedSender and new allowedsender simultaneously
findings.test_recommendation: Run allowed-sender-modern.sh and existing legacy allowed-sender-*.sh tests to confirm no regression
